title: what would you improve first about the visuals?
author: Civil-Ad-7646
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’m making Beyond the Cradle on my own in Godot, inspired by Satisfactory and Dyson Sphere Program.

The idea is to start with a small colony and build up a network of factories across planets and moons, shipping resources between them. AI tools have been part of my development process, helping with code review and debugging.

This video shows some of the worlds I’ve been working on. The game is still in development, and I’m trying to figure out where to focus the next round of visual improvements.

If you could change one thing about the visuals, what would you change first, and why? I’m especially interested in how the building models fit with the terrain, and whether they’re easy to make out as the camera pulls back. Feel free to point to a specific moment in the video.

If the game looks interesting to you, a wishlist would help me a lot:  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4464270/Beyond\_the\_Cradle/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4464270/Beyond_the_Cradle/)

Thanks for checking it out!

comments.author: joeld42
comments.body:
This is a pretty strong start! You have a strong visual identity, a controlled color palette, and interesting variety in the biomes. 

I think overall the biggest comment I have is a lot of the terrain looks good but it's not intentional. There are a few features: craters, lava flows that is is clear what they are, but there are a lot of "green blobs" where it's not clear if that's meant to be a forest, or a grassland, or a algae mat.  Are the "blue blobs" oceans? or glaciers? or barren rock?  Even if it's procedural you can find ways to make the patterns look more specific, with edge patterns, faint textures, a few scattered details, etc. 

Some of the background skybox detail can be distracting and compete with the game elements. They look really cool but might not serve gameplay. 

Adding more "areas of rest" on the planet surface, it's not overly detailed but it's kind of uniformly detailed, some dense areas and some empty space would give it more breathing room, like whitespace on a page.

Maybe it's just the camera in your video, but it feels like this spends a lot of time showing the empty space around the cities. Your game is a city-builder, not a screensaver, so make it about the stuff the player has built. 

Also the lighting on the planet terrain looks really flat. I think you could push that a lot further to show more of the form of the terrain without losing the illustrated look, but that could be tricky and make it look worse too so try it out but use your judgement.

I think emissives and lights on player's buildings on the night-side of the planets could look cool, and help draw their eye to the buildings.
